title: A border follows the shape it is on, not the box around it
goal: A Border on a drawing, a shape, a path, an arrow, a group or a cut-out picture runs round the thing itself, the way a Stroke does in Photoshop and Figma: round the package's outline, along the arrow. A plain box round the layer is still available when that is what the person wants, but it is no longer the only kind.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20, on Ask's 'package in some clouds' drawing: 'i wanted a border around the box. I selected the product package. added a border effect. It created a box border, and not one that followed the outline of the shape. Ideally, we follow the outline of the shape. Same thing for arrows. borders are borders, not always boxes.' In the picture the package is a group of 8 paths and the 2 px Outside border is the group's frame rectangle.

Cause, from code: Sources/PhotonzCore/BorderFollows.swift:20-22 says only a label has letters to follow and everything else (picture, shape, frame, group) 'has a box and nothing else, so its rings follow the box whatever this says and the panel never asks (Layer.boxBorders)'. That rule was written for labels on 2026-09-08 and never revisited for drawn shapes. Reuse the label's choice (BorderFollows: letters or box) as shape or box. The renderer has ContourTracer (Sources/PhotonzRender) and OutlineStroke.swift. Watch the composite path's cost (CLAUDE.md perf note) and the SVG exporter's border path.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: pick the drawn package (a group of paths), add a Border, and record the rectangle it draws (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-border-is-a-box.png is the user's)

On a shape, path, arrow, line or group, a Border follows the outline: Outside, Inside and Centre mean what they mean in Photoshop's Stroke, round corners stay round, an arrow's shaft and head are outlined as one shape, and a group is outlined as the union of its parts (one ring round the whole package, not one per face)

On a picture with transparency (a cut-out, a sticker, a PNG with an alpha edge) it follows the visible edge, traced from the alpha (ContourTracer exists); on an opaque rectangular picture or screenshot it is the box, as today

Each Border row says which it follows (the shape, or the box) where both make sense, the way a label's border already offers its letters or its box, and the default is the shape for anything that is not a rectangle

Width, offset, colour and position act on the followed outline; multiple borders stack outward in order; it draws the same on the canvas, in PNG, in SVG (as a real stroke or an outline path) and in MP4, compared by render
Performance: dragging the Width slider on the package stays inside a frame (16 ms) on this Mac, measured

A walk for a group, an arrow, a cut-out picture and a plain screenshot, and an audit under queue/audits/ with before and after. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced at Next defaults with Scripts/playtest/border-follows-the-shape-walk.json (no flags): a 2px Outside Border on a group of 2 ovals + a box, on an arrow, and on a cut-out star PNG each draws a rectangle round the layer's box (queue/audits/2026-10-20-border-follows-the-shape-before.png). Paths and ovals already follow their outline (layer.path / ringShape .ellipse).

Adversarial review before building: a Photoshop user expects Stroke to follow the layer's pixels, a group's stroke to go round the union of its parts, and Inside to eat into the shape with no seams between parts; Figma has no group stroke, so Photoshop is the model. Risk found: overlapping parts drawn in opposite directions cancel to holes under the winding rule, so parts are merged with real unions, not normalised together.

Chose to reuse the label's choice (BorderFollows) as Shape/Box rather than a new setting: the saved word stays 'letters' so every file opens as before, and every non-rectangle defaults to the shape. Chose vector outlines (union of parts, arrow shaft+head, marching-squares trace of a picture's alpha) fed to the existing path-ring baker over an image-space dilation, because it is exact, matches SVG export, and costs the same as a box ring.

Measured: Width drag on an 8-part package, full 1440x1024 canvas at 2x: 8.3 ms median, 9.0 ms worst per frame (box ring 8.3 ms); outline merged once per drag (ShapeBorderDragCostTests). Scripts/test.sh: 14153 tests passed. Walks green: border-follows-the-shape (new), label-border-follows, two-way-effect-setting-reads-mixed, appearance-and-effects-dropdowns-open-on-a-click, border-off-keeps-its-row, copy-a-look, ellipse-border, border-effect, border-offset, effects-say-their-reach, a-border-on-a-full-frame-picture-shows, border-follows-the-path.

border-follows-the-path walk failed at step 46 on the code WITHOUT this change too (stashed Sources, rebuilt probe, same failure): a new shape is drawn in the last look, so the line already wore the triangle's border and adding one made two Width sliders. Fixed the walk, not the app.

Looked at the pictures: before (boxes round group, arrow, star), after doc render (one ring round the cloud, along the arrow, round the star, box round the opaque tile), all six window captures, and the star edge at 4x (first trace was a half-pixel staircase wobble; replaced the whole-pixel trace with marching squares and it is now smooth and flush).

left rough (not filed, no person-visible defect yet): a label inside a group counts as its box for the group's ring; a cropped or clip-zoomed picture rings its box; several borders overlap rather than stack outward (unchanged behaviour, Offset stacks them); open path with Follows: Box still hides Position.

A Border on a group, arrow, line or cut-out picture follows the shape (union of parts, shaft+head, alpha edge); opaque pictures/rectangles/frames stay boxed; each row offers Follows: Shape/Box; SVG matches. Commit c285edbc. Verified: 14153 tests green incl. new ShapeOutline/PictureEdge/ShapeBorderRender tests; walk border-follows-the-shape at Next defaults (6 real window captures); Width drag 8.3 ms median at 2x.
